title: How Long Do Night Guards Last? (Based on Real Durability Tests)
h1: How Long Do Night Guards Last?
meta: We tracked the exact lifespan of OTC and custom night guards. Find out how long they actually last before you need a replacement.
target_kw: how long do night guards last

body_sections.h2: Average Lifespan of Different Night Guards
body_sections.html: While dentists often quote 2 to 5 years for custom acrylic night guards, over-the-counter boil-and-bite models generally last between 1 and 6 months depending on the severity of your grinding [1]. Soft EVA guards tend to wear out the fastest, as heavy bruxers can chew through them in a matter of weeks.

citations.claim: General guidelines for mouthguard replacement and lifespan

faq: When should I replace my night guard?
You should replace your night guard if it has visible holes, deep indentations that affect your bite, cracks, or if it no longer fits securely on your teeth.

title: How to Stop Grinding Teeth in Your Sleep (Science-Backed Methods)
h1: How to Stop Grinding Teeth in Your Sleep
meta: Discover effective strategies to reduce sleep bruxism, from stress management to sleep hygiene and physical therapy.
target_kw: how to stop grinding teeth in sleep

body_sections.html: Stopping sleep bruxism entirely is difficult because it is centrally regulated by the nervous system. However, managing it often involves a combination of stress reduction techniques, improving sleep hygiene, avoiding alcohol and caffeine before bed, and wearing a protective occlusal splint to prevent dental wear [1].

citations.claim: Occlusal splints for treating sleep bruxism

title: What Causes Bruxism? Understanding Teeth Grinding
meta: Explore the primary causes of teeth grinding, including stress, genetics, medications, and sleep disorders.

body_sections.html: Bruxism is a multifactorial condition. While historical theories blamed a misaligned bite (malocclusion), modern consensus points to central nervous system factors. High stress, anxiety, sleep apnea, and certain medications (like SSRIs) are strong correlating factors in adult populations [1] [2].

citations.claim: International consensus on the assessment of bruxism

title: Soft vs Hard Night Guard: Which is Better for Teeth Grinding?
meta: Comparing soft, dual-laminate, and hard acrylic night guards. Learn which material is right for your level of bruxism.

body_sections.html: Soft night guards are typically made of EVA (ethylene vinyl acetate) and are comfortable but can actually encourage more chewing in some heavy grinders. Hard acrylic guards are rigid and highly durable, making them the standard recommendation for severe bruxism to protect the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and teeth from extreme pressure [1].

citations.claim: International consensus on the assessment of bruxism

title: Night Guard vs Mouthguard: Key Differences Explained
meta: Can you use a sports mouthguard for sleep bruxism? We explain the critical differences in design, material, and function.

body_sections.html: A sports mouthguard is thick, bulky, and designed to absorb sudden impact to the teeth and gums. A night guard is made of rigid or semi-rigid plastic to withstand sustained grinding pressure over hours and to protect the enamel without disrupting your natural bite [1]. Wearing a sports mouthguard to sleep can cause jaw pain or shift your bite.

citations.claim: Night guards vs sports mouthguards: design and intended use differ significantly

title: How to Clean a Night Guard: Daily and Weekly Routines
h1: How to Clean a Night Guard
meta: Step-by-step guide on how to properly clean and sanitize your night guard to prevent bacterial buildup and odors.
target_kw: how to clean a night guard

body_sections.html: Rinse your night guard with cold or warm water immediately after removal. Brush it lightly with a soft toothbrush (without abrasive toothpaste). For deep cleaning, use non-abrasive denture cleaning tablets or a mild soap [1]. Never use hot water, as it can warp the plastic.

citations.claim: Proper care and hygiene of dental appliances including night guards

title: Is Your Night Guard Making Your Jaw Hurt? Here’s Why
h1: Why Does My Night Guard Make My Jaw Hurt?
meta: Experiencing jaw pain after wearing your night guard? Learn about bite misalignment, clenching habits, and when to see a dentist.

body_sections.html: Some mild discomfort during the first few days is normal as your mouth adjusts. However, if your night guard causes persistent jaw pain or headaches, it may be incorrectly fitted or too thick, disrupting your natural resting bite [1]. Over-the-counter boil-and-bite models are particularly prone to uneven occlusal surfaces.

citations.claim: Occlusal splints for treating sleep bruxism
